questions.explanation: Ideal divisor = 84,000,000 ÷ (16 × 115,200) = 84,000,000 ÷ 1,843,200 ≈ 45.57, nearest integer 46. Actual = 84,000,000 ÷ (16 × 46) = 84,000,000 ÷ 736 ≈ 114,130 baud. Error = (114,130 − 115,200) ÷ 115,200 ≈ −0.93%, jo chal jaayega. Traps: round ki jagah truncate karna (45 → +1.27%, thoda zyada error), divisor round karke baud wahi maan lena (0%), ya sign ulta likhna (actual desired se kam hai, isliye minus).

questions.question: 16-bit millisecond counter wrap ke paas hai. `start = 65000` par 1000 ms ka timeout shuru hua, aur ab `now = 500` hai. Dono checks kya denge?
options: Dono 0, kyunki 500 abhi bhi 65000 se chhota hai
Dono 1, kyunki counter wrap ho chuka hai
questions.explanation: `now - start` = 500 − 65000 = −64500, jo `uint16_t` me cast hokar −64500 + 65536 = 1036 banta hai: 536 ms wrap se pehle + 500 baad. 1036 ≥ 1000, to `ok_check` = 1. `start + delay` `int` me 66000 hai, aur 500 ≥ 66000 false, to `bad_check` = 0 aur timeout kabhi detect nahi hoga (kyunki `now` kabhi 66000 tak nahi pahunch sakta). Traps: wrap ko ignore karna (dono 0), maan lena ki wrap sab theek kar deta hai (dono 1), ya deadline ko 16 bits me wrap karke (66000 − 65536 = 464) us 464 ko beeta hua time samajhna.

questions.question: 1 MHz timer par input capture se ye values mili: rising edge 1200, falling edge 1950, agla rising edge 3700 (beech me koi wrap nahi). Signal ki frequency aur duty cycle kya hai?
questions.explanation: Period = rising se rising = 3700 − 1200 = 2500 ticks = 2500 µs, to frequency = 1,000,000 ÷ 2500 = 400 Hz. High time = falling − rising = 1950 − 1200 = 750 µs, duty = 750 ÷ 2500 = 30%. Traps: low time ko duty lena (1750 ÷ 2500 = 70%), µs ko ms jaisa padh kar 2.5 kHz bolna, ya falling se rising (1750) ko period maanna (≈ 571 Hz, 43%).

questions.question: Har 2 ms ke cycle me firmware do kaam karta hai: I2C (400 kHz) se ek sensor read jisme address byte + 6 data bytes hain (har byte 9 clocks, START/STOP ignore), aur UART (115200 baud, 8N1) par 20 bytes ka log. Total bus time kitna hai, aur kya ye 2 ms me fit hota hai?
questions.explanation: I2C: 7 bytes × 9 = 63 clocks ÷ 400,000 = 157.5 µs. UART: 20 × 10 = 200 bits ÷ 115,200 ≈ 1736 µs. Total ≈ 1894 µs ≈ 1.89 ms < 2 ms, margin sirf ~0.1 ms. Traps: dono me 8 bits per byte lena (140 + 1389 µs ≈ 1.53 ms), I2C ko 100 kHz par ginna (630 + 1736 ≈ 2.37 ms), ya I2C ka time chhod dena (≈ 1.74 ms).

weeks.title: Firmware Design: Super-Loops, State Machines and Ring Buffers
weeks.summary: Is week aap super-loop architecture aur non-blocking tasks, C me enum + switch se state machine, layered drivers/HAL aur modular design, aur ISR se main tak data le jaane wala ring buffer seekhoge.
concepts: **Super-loop**: `main` me pehle init, phir `while (1) { task_a(); task_b(); task_c(); }`. Koi OS nahi, samajhna aasaan. Kamzori: agar ek task block kare (busy-wait delay), to baaki saare tasks bhi ruk jaate hain, aur kisi event ka response time poore loop ke worst-case time jitna ho sakta hai. Urgent kaam ISR me (sirf flag set karke) aur baaki loop me.

**Non-blocking timing**: busy-wait delay ki jagah start tick yaad rakho aur har loop me check karo: `if ((now - start) >= PERIOD) { start = now; do_work(); }`. Isse alag-alag tasks alag rates par chal sakte hain aur loop kabhi atakta nahi.

**Finite State Machine (FSM)**: system ek samay par ek hi state me hota hai aur events se doosri state me jaata hai. C me states ke liye `enum` aur logic ke liye `switch (state)`. Har state me sirf woh events handle karo jo wahan matter karte hain; baaki events ignore. FSM se code predictable aur testable banta hai.

**Layered design aur HAL**: application → device driver (jaise `temp_read()`) → HAL (`gpio_write()`, `i2c_read()`) → registers. Upar ki layers hardware details nahi jaanti, isliye naye MCU par port karne ke liye mainly sabse neeche ki layer badalni padti hai, aur PC par testing ke liye HAL ko fake (mock) kiya ja sakta hai.

**Modular C**: har module ka `.h` (public functions aur types) aur `.c` (implementation). Module ke private globals aur helper functions `static` banao taaki doosri files unhe seedha na chhu sakein. Chhote, saaf interfaces bugs kam karte hain.

**Ring (circular) buffer**: fixed array + `head` (yahan likho) + `tail` (yahan se padho). Producer (jaise UART RX ISR) head par likhta hai, consumer (main loop) tail se padhta hai, aur index `(i + 1) % SIZE` se wrap hota hai. Empty: `head == tail`. Ek slot khaali rakhne wale design me full: `(head + 1) % SIZE == tail`, isliye maximum SIZE − 1 items. Items ki ginti = (head − tail + SIZE) % SIZE.

**Power-of-two trick**: SIZE 2 ki power ho (8, 16, 64) to `% SIZE` ki jagah `& (SIZE - 1)` likh sakte ho, jo fast hai. SIZE 2 ki power na ho to ye mask galat indices deta hai, isliye ye trick sirf power-of-two sizes ke saath.

**Single producer, single consumer**: agar sirf ISR `head` badle aur sirf main `tail` badle, to ring buffer bina lock ke safe chalta hai (indices `volatile` aur ek hi instruction me read/write hone wale size ke hon).

example.problem: SIZE = 8 ka ring buffer khaali hai (head = tail = 0). 'a', 'b', 'c' push karo, phir ek pop karo. head, tail, popped value aur bache items batao.
steps: Push 'a': buf[0] = 'a', head = 1.
Push 'b': buf[1] = 'b', head = 2.
Push 'c': buf[2] = 'c', head = 3.
Pop: buf[tail] = buf[0] = 'a' milta hai, tail = 1.
Answer: **head = 3, tail = 1, popped 'a', 2 items bache**.

mistakes: Super-loop ke kisi task me busy-wait delay daalna. Poora system us delay jitna slow ho jaata hai; tick-based non-blocking check use karo.
Ring buffer me items ginne ke liye `head - tail` seedha lena. head wrap hokar tail se chhota ho sakta hai; `(head - tail + SIZE) % SIZE` lo.
Non-power-of-two SIZE ke saath `& (SIZE - 1)` lagana. Index kuch hi values ke beech ghoomta reh jaata hai aur data overwrite hota hai.
revision: Super-loop me kuch bhi block na kare; urgent kaam ISR + flag.
FSM = `enum` states + `switch`; har state me sirf relevant events.
HAL/driver layers se porting aur testing aasaan.
Ring buffer: empty `head == tail`, full `(head + 1) % SIZE == tail`, capacity SIZE − 1.
`& (SIZE - 1)` sirf jab SIZE 2 ki power ho.

questions.question: Ek super-loop (bina OS) me teen tasks hain. Ek task ke andar kisi ne `delay_ms(500);` (busy-wait) daal diya. Iska kya asar hoga?
options: Har loop iteration me baaki tasks ki baari bhi kam se kam 500 ms der se aayegi
Sirf wahi task slow hoga, baaki tasks parallel chalte rahenge
Compiler busy-wait ko optimise karke hata dega
Saare interrupts hamesha ke liye disable ho jaayenge
questions.explanation: Super-loop me tasks ek ke baad ek chalte hain; koi parallelism nahi hai. Jab ek task 500 ms busy-wait karta hai, loop wahin ruk jaata hai aur baaki tasks ka response 500 ms+ late ho jaata hai. Interrupts phir bhi chalte hain (ISR theek hain), par main-loop ka kaam ruka rehta hai. Trap: OS jaisa parallel execution maan lena.

questions.question: Sensor driver ko seedha registers ki jagah ek HAL layer (`i2c_read()`, `gpio_write()`) ke upar likhne ka sabse bada fayda kya hai?
options: Code hamesha registers wale code se fast chalega
Program ka Flash usage zero ho jaata hai
Naye MCU par port karne ke liye mainly HAL layer badalni padti hai, driver aur app logic waise hi rehte hain
Interrupts ki zaroorat khatam ho jaati hai
questions.explanation: Layering ka maqsad hardware details ko ek jagah band karna hai. Driver sirf HAL functions jaanta hai, isliye chip badalne par HAL ka naya implementation likho aur upar ka code same chalega; PC par testing ke liye HAL ko mock bhi kar sakte ho. Extra layer se code thoda slow ya bada ho sakta hai, fast nahi (trap).

questions.question: SIZE = 8 ke ring buffer me abhi `head = 3` aur `tail = 6` hai (head = agla write index, tail = agla read index). Buffer me kitne items hain?
questions.explanation: Count = (head − tail + SIZE) % SIZE = (3 − 6 + 8) % 8 = 5. Head wrap hokar aage nikal chuka hai: items index 6, 7, 0, 1, 2 par hain, yaani 5. Trap: 6 − 3 = 3 lena, jo khaali slots ki ginti ke kareeb hai, items ki nahi. -3 tab aata jab `+ SIZE` aur `%` bhool gaye.

questions.question: Ek ring buffer ye full/empty checks use karta hai. Ek samay par isme maximum kitne items store ho sakte hain?
questions.explanation: Agar saare 16 slots bhar dete to head ghoom kar tail ke barabar ho jaata, aur `head == tail` empty jaisa dikhta, full aur empty me fark nahi rehta. Isliye ye design ek slot hamesha khaali rakhta hai: full tab jab head, tail se ek peeche ho. Maximum = SIZE − 1 = 15. Trap: array size 16 ko hi capacity maan lena.

questions.question: State machine shuru me IDLE me hai. Events is order me aate hain: 'P', 'S', 'P', 'S', 'X', 'P'. Saare events ke baad state kya hogi?
options: Compile error, kyunki `switch` me `enum` use nahi ho sakta
questions.explanation: Trace: IDLE me 'P' ignore → IDLE. 'S' → RUNNING. 'P' → PAUSED. 'S' → RUNNING. 'X' → IDLE. Aakhri 'P' IDLE me ignore hota hai → IDLE. Trap: aakhri event 'P' dekh kar PAUSED bolna; FSM me event ka asar current state par depend karta hai. `enum` values integers hain, `switch` me bilkul valid.

questions.question: Ek programmer ne ring buffer index ke liye power-of-two trick use ki, par SIZE 6 rakh diya. Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: SIZE − 1 = 5 = 101 (binary). idx = 0: (1) & 101 = 1. idx = 1: (2 = 010) & 101 = 0. Phir wahi cycle: 1, 0, 1. Index sirf 0 aur 1 ke beech ghoomta hai, baaki slots kabhi use nahi hote. `& (SIZE - 1)` tabhi `% SIZE` ke barabar hai jab SIZE 2 ki power ho. Trap: maan lena ki ye `% 6` jaisa kaam karega (1 2 3 4 5).

questions.question: Ek module ki `.c` file me helper function `static int crc_step(int x)` likha hai. Is `static` ka kya matlab hai?
options: Ye function har call ke baad apni saari values bhool jaata hai
Ye function kabhi bhi interrupt ke andar se call nahi ho sakta
Ye function sirf usi `.c` file ke andar se call ho sakta hai
Ye function poore program me sirf ek hi baar chal sakta hai
questions.explanation: File-level `static` function ya global ko private bana deta hai: wo sirf apni `.c` file me dikhta hai, doosri files use seedha call nahi kar sakti. Isse module ka interface chhota aur saaf rehta hai. Iska interrupts ya 'ek baar chalne' se koi lena-dena nahi. Trap: function-level `static` ko local `static` variable ke matlab (value yaad rakhna) se mix karna.

questions.question: Ring buffer (`head` = agla write index, `tail` = agla read index) kab khaali maana jaata hai?
questions.explanation: Jab write aur read index barabar hon, to padhne ke liye kuch bacha nahi: empty. `(head + 1) % SIZE == tail` full ki condition hai (ek slot khaali rakhne wale design me). `head == 0` sirf position hai, aur `tail > head` wrap ke baad bhi ho sakta hai jab buffer me items hon. Trap: full aur empty conditions ulat dena.

questions.question: C me finite state machine likhne ka sabse common aur saaf tareeka kya hai?
options: Har state ke liye ek alag `while (1)` loop likhna
States ko random numbers se represent karna
Har event par `delay_ms()` daal kar state badalna
States ke liye `enum` aur logic ke liye `switch (state)`
questions.explanation: `enum` se states ke naam saaf rehte hain, aur `switch` me har `case` ek state ka logic hota hai jo sirf usi state ke events handle karta hai. Har state ka alag infinite loop baaki tasks ko rok deta hai, random numbers padhne me mushkil hain, aur delays FSM ko blocking bana dete hain. Trap: FSM ko blocking loops ka set samajhna.

questions.question: SIZE = 32 ke ring buffer me `head = 7` aur `tail = 20` hai. Buffer me kitne items hain?
questions.explanation: Count = (head − tail + SIZE) % SIZE = (7 − 20 + 32) % 32 = 19. Items index 20 se 31 (12) aur 0 se 6 (7) tak hain: 12 + 7 = 19. Traps: tail − head = 13 lena, `+ SIZE` bhool jaana (-13), ya wrap ke baad wala hissa (0–6) na ginna (12).

questions.question: Super-loop me ye code har iteration chalta hai, aur `ms` har millisecond badhne wala tick counter hai. LED ki blink frequency (ek on + ek off = ek blink) kya hogi?
questions.explanation: LED har 250 ms par toggle hota hai: 250 ms on, 250 ms off, to ek poora blink 500 ms ka, yaani 1 ÷ 0.5 s = 2 Hz. Traps: toggle rate ko blink rate maan lena (1 ÷ 0.25 s = 4 Hz), period ko 1 s lena (1 Hz), ya 250 ko seedha Hz likh dena.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Ek slot khaali rakhne wale design me SIZE 4 me maximum 3 items. 'a', 'b', 'c' slots 0–2 me (head = 3). 'd' ke liye next = 0 = tail, to full: 'd' drop. Pop → 'a' (tail = 1). Push 'e': next = 0 ≠ 1, to buf[3] = 'e', head = 0. Teen pops: 'b', 'c', 'e'. Output abce. Traps: maan lena ki 4 items fit honge (abcd), drop pehle item ka hota hai (bcde), ya pop LIFO jaisa hai.

questions.question: Door-lock state machine shuru me LOCKED hai aur `wrong = 0`. Events is order me aate hain: 'W', 'W', 'C', 'L', 'W', 'W', 'W', 'C'. Saare events ke baad state aur `wrong` kya honge?
questions.explanation: Trace: W → wrong 1, W → 2 (dono LOCKED). C → UNLOCKED, wrong 0. L → LOCKED. W → 1, W → 2, W → 3, aur 3 ≥ 3 to ALARM. Aakhri C ALARM me ignore hota hai (sirf 'R' nikaalta hai). Final: ALARM, wrong = 3. Traps: maan lena ki sahi code ALARM se bhi unlock kar dega (UNLOCKED), ALARM ki transition miss karna (LOCKED), ya saare W gin lena, chahe C ne count reset kiya ho (5).

questions.question: Super-loop me teen tasks har iteration chalte hain: `task_a()` 2 ms, `task_b()` 5 ms, `task_c()` 3 ms. ISR sirf ek flag set karta hai, jise `task_a()` apni shuruaat me check karta hai. Galti se `task_b()` me `delay_ms(20);` (busy-wait) bhi hai. Flag set hone se handle hone tak worst-case latency kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Worst case: flag theek us waqt set hota hai jab task A use check kar chuka ho. Ab baaki A (2 ms), B (5 + 20 = 25 ms) aur C (3 ms) chalne ke baad hi A dobara check karega: 2 + 25 + 3 = 30 ms. Traps: delay ko ignore karna (10 ms), sirf B ka time lena (25 ms), ya sirf delay ginna (20 ms). Busy-wait poore loop ka response time badha deta hai.

questions.question: Do ring buffers ke items power-of-two trick se gine ja rahe hain, ek SIZE 16 ka aur ek galti se SIZE 12 ka. 32-bit `unsigned` par is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Unsigned me 2 − 13 wrap hokar 0xFFFFFFF5 banta hai; & 15 = 0x5 = 5, jo (2 − 13 + 16) % 16 = 5 se match karta hai. 2 − 9 = 0xFFFFFFF9; & 11 (binary 1011) = 1001 = 9, jabki sahi count (2 − 9 + 12) % 12 = 5 hai. Power-of-two na ho to mask galat answer deta hai. Traps: dono ko sahi maan lena (5 5), unsigned me negative print hona (-11 -7), ya tail − head ginna (11 7).

weeks.title: Real-Time Operating Systems: Tasks, Scheduling and Synchronisation
weeks.summary: Is week aap RTOS me tasks aur unki states, preemptive priority scheduling aur tick-based delays, semaphore, mutex aur queue ka sahi use, priority inversion, aur rate-monotonic utilisation check seekhoge.
concepts: **Real-time ka matlab**: sirf sahi result nahi, sahi samay par sahi result. **Hard real-time** me deadline miss = failure (airbag, motor control), **soft real-time** me miss chal jaata hai par quality girti hai (audio, display). RTOS ka kaam hai predictable (deterministic) scheduling dena.

**Task**: ek independent function (aksar infinite loop) jiska apna stack hota hai. States: **Running** (abhi CPU par), **Ready** (chal sakta hai, CPU ka wait), **Blocked** (delay, semaphore ya queue ka wait), **Suspended**. Har task ka stack alag RAM leta hai, isliye stack size soch kar do.

**Preemptive priority scheduler**: hamesha sabse high priority wala Ready task chalta hai. Koi higher-priority task Ready hote hi (jaise ISR ne semaphore diya) scheduler current task ko turant preempt kar deta hai. Same priority ke tasks time-slicing (round-robin) se baari-baari chalte hain. Task badalne ko **context switch** kehte hain (registers save/restore).

**Tick aur delays**: scheduler ek periodic **tick** interrupt (jaise SysTick, 1 kHz) se time ginta hai. Delay function (jaise `vTaskDelay(n)`) task ko n ticks ke liye Blocked kar deta hai aur CPU doosre tasks ko milta hai, busy-wait nahi hota. Time = ticks ÷ tick rate: 100 Hz tick par 50 ticks = 500 ms. Fixed-rate periodic tasks ke liye absolute 'delay until' use karo taaki time drift na ho.

**Semaphore aur mutex**: **binary semaphore** signalling ke liye hai: ISR 'give' karta hai, task 'take' par wait karta hai (interrupt ka bhaari kaam task me). **Counting semaphore** N resources ya pending events ginta hai. **Mutex** shared resource (UART, I2C bus, shared struct) ki mutual exclusion ke liye hai: jo task lock kare wahi unlock kare, aur usually **priority inheritance** ke saath aata hai. ISR me mutex kabhi mat lo.

**Queue**: tasks (aur ISR se task) ke beech data bhejne ka safe tareeka. Items copy hoke jaate hain aur queue ki length fixed hoti hai. Queue full ho to sender timeout tak block hota hai (timeout 0 ho to turant fail), aur queue empty ho to receiver block hota hai.

**Priority inversion**: Low task L ne mutex liya. High task H usi mutex par block ho gaya. Ab Medium task M (jise mutex nahi chahiye) L ko preempt kar leta hai, L mutex chhod nahi paata, aur H asal me M ki wajah se ruka rehta hai. Fix: **priority inheritance**, jisme L temporarily H ki priority le leta hai jab tak mutex na chhode.

**Rate-monotonic (RM) check**: periodic tasks me chhote period wale ko zyada priority. Utilisation U = Σ (Cᵢ ÷ Tᵢ), jahan C = execution time, T = period. Agar U ≤ n × (2 ka n-th root − 1) (n = 3 ke liye ≈ 0.78, bahut tasks ke liye ≈ 0.69), to RM saari deadlines guarantee karta hai. Bound se zyada U ka matlab zaroori fail nahi, bas guarantee nahi; U > 1 matlab pakka overload.

example.problem: Tick 1 kHz hai. Task A (high priority) har 10 ms par jaagta hai aur 2 ms CPU leta hai, phir 'delay until' se agle period tak block. Task B (low priority) hamesha Ready rehta hai (background kaam). B ko CPU ka kitna hissa milta hai, aur t = 10 ms par kya hota hai?
steps: t = 0 par A Ready hai aur higher priority hai, isliye 0–2 ms A chalta hai.
2 ms par A block hota hai, B chalta hai 2–10 ms.
t = 10 ms par tick A ko Ready banata hai; A ki priority zyada hai, to B preempt hota hai aur A 10–12 ms chalta hai.
Har 10 ms me A ko 2 ms, B ko 8 ms milte hain.
A ka utilisation = 2 ÷ 10 = 0.2.
Answer: **B ko 80% CPU milta hai; t = 10 ms par A, B ko preempt karta hai**.

mistakes: Task ke andar busy-wait loop se delay karna. Isse low priority tasks ko CPU milta hi nahi; RTOS ka delay use karo jo task ko Blocked karta hai.
Shared resource ke liye binary semaphore use karna. Usme ownership aur priority inheritance nahi hote; mutual exclusion ke liye mutex lo.
ISR se blocking call (mutex take, queue send with wait) karna. ISR block nahi ho sakta; ISR-safe 'from ISR' versions use karo.
revision: Highest-priority Ready task chalta hai; higher priority Ready hote hi preempt.
Delay ticks ÷ tick rate = time; delay task ko Blocked karta hai.
Semaphore = signalling, mutex = mutual exclusion (+ priority inheritance), queue = data.
Priority inversion: L ke paas mutex, M beech me, H atka; fix inheritance.
RM: U = Σ C/T; n = 3 par bound ≈ 0.78.

questions.question: Preemptive priority-based RTOS scheduler me kisi bhi samay kaunsa task CPU par chalta hai?
options: Jo task sabse pehle create hua tha
Ready state wale tasks me sabse high priority wala
Blocked tasks me sabse high priority wala
questions.explanation: Scheduler sirf Ready tasks me se chunta hai, aur unme sabse high priority wala chalta hai. Blocked task (delay ya semaphore ka wait) chahe kitni bhi high priority ka ho, tab tak nahi chalta jab tak Ready na ho. Creation order ya stack size ka priority se lena-dena nahi.

questions.question: Do tasks ek hi UART par messages print karte hain, aur dono ke messages aapas me mix nahi hone chahiye. Iske liye sabse sahi RTOS primitive kaunsa hai?
options: Ek binary semaphore jise ISR give karta hai
Ek counting semaphore jiska initial count 10 ho
questions.explanation: Shared resource ko ek samay par ek hi task use kare, ye mutual exclusion hai, aur iske liye mutex bana hai: ownership hoti hai (jo lock kare wahi unlock kare) aur priority inheritance se priority inversion kam hota hai. Plain flag me check aur set ke beech task switch ho sakta hai (race). Count 10 wala semaphore ek saath 10 tasks ko andar aane dega.

questions.question: RTOS ka tick rate 100 Hz hai. Ek task `delay(50)` call karta hai, jahan argument ticks me hai. Task lagbhag kitni der Blocked rahega?
questions.explanation: 100 Hz tick = har tick 10 ms. 50 ticks × 10 ms = 500 ms. Trap: argument ko seedha milliseconds maan lena (50 ms); ye tabhi sahi hota jab tick 1 kHz hota. Isiliye portable code ticks ko time se convert karne wala macro use karta hai.

questions.question: Task L (low priority) ne ek mutex liya. Phir task H (high) Ready hua aur usi mutex par block ho gaya. Ab task M (medium, jise mutex nahi chahiye) Ready hota hai aur bahut der tak chalta hai. Priority inheritance ke BINA kya hoga?
options: H turant M ko preempt karke chalega, kyunki H ki priority sabse zyada hai
Ye deadlock hai: L aur H dono hamesha ke liye atak jaayenge chahe M ho ya na ho
M, L ko preempt karega, L mutex release nahi kar paayega, aur H asal me M ki wajah se rukta rahega
H ke block hote hi L apne aap mutex chhod dega
questions.explanation: H Blocked hai (mutex ka wait), isliye Ready tasks me M sabse high hai aur woh L ko preempt kar leta hai. L ko CPU nahi milta, to mutex nahi chhutta, aur H ek medium task ki wajah se der tak ruka rehta hai. Ye priority inversion hai. Priority inheritance me L ki priority temporarily H jitni ho jaati, M usse preempt na kar paata, aur L jaldi mutex chhod deta. Ye deadlock nahi hai: M khatam hote hi sab chal padta hai.

questions.question: Ek queue ki length 5 hai aur abhi khaali hai. Ek high-priority producer task lagataar 8 items bhejta hai, har send ka timeout 0, aur is beech consumer task ko chalne ka mauka nahi milta. Kya hoga?
options: Saare 8 items chale jaayenge, koi send fail nahi hoga
5 sends successful honge, aakhri 3 fail honge
Queue ke overflow se pehle 5 items overwrite hokar sirf aakhri 5 bachenge, aur sab sends successful dikhenge
questions.explanation: Queue me sirf 5 jagah hain aur consumer kuch nikaal nahi raha. Pehle 5 sends jagah paate hain. 6th se queue full hai; timeout 0 hai, to sender wait nahi karta aur send turant fail (error return) hota hai, isliye 3 fail. Normal RTOS queue purana data chupchap overwrite nahi karta. Trap: queue ko infinite maan lena.

questions.question: Teen periodic tasks rate-monotonic priorities ke saath chal rahe hain: T1 (C = 2 ms, T = 10 ms), T2 (C = 4 ms, T = 20 ms), T3 (C = 10 ms, T = 40 ms). 3 tasks ke liye RM utilisation bound ≈ 0.78 hai. Sahi conclusion kya hai?
options: U ≈ 0.23; bound se kam, isliye schedulable
U = 0.65; bound se zyada, isliye deadlines miss hongi
U = 0.80; bound se zyada, isliye guarantee nahi
U = 0.65; bound se kam, isliye RM saari deadlines guarantee karta hai
questions.explanation: U = 2/10 + 4/20 + 10/40 = 0.20 + 0.20 + 0.25 = 0.65. Ye 0.78 se kam hai, isliye Liu–Layland test pass: RM ke saath saari deadlines guaranteed. Traps: saare C jod kar saare T se divide karna (16/70 ≈ 0.23, ye galat formula hai); 10/40 ko 0.4 padh lena (0.80); ya 0.65 aur 0.78 ki comparison ulti kar dena.

questions.question: Ek task semaphore ka 100 ms timeout ke saath wait kar raha hai, aur abhi tak kisi ne semaphore give nahi kiya. Task kis state me hai?
questions.explanation: Jo task kisi event (semaphore, queue, delay) ka wait kar raha ho wo Blocked hai: use CPU nahi milta jab tak event na aaye ya timeout na ho. Ready ka matlab hai 'chal sakta hai, bas CPU ka intezaar', aur Suspended tab hota hai jab task ko explicitly rok diya jaaye. Trap: wait karne wale task ko Ready samajhna.

questions.question: RTOS me `vTaskDelay(100)` jaisa delay call karne par kya hota hai?
options: Task 100 ticks tak busy-wait loop me CPU ghumata rehta hai
Poora scheduler aur saare tasks 100 ticks ke liye ruk jaate hain
Saare interrupts 100 ticks ke liye band ho jaate hain
Task 100 ticks Blocked rehta hai aur CPU doosre tasks ko milta hai
questions.explanation: RTOS delay task ko Blocked state me daal deta hai aur scheduler doosre Ready tasks chalata hai; tick interrupt time ginta rehta hai, aur time poora hone par task phir Ready hota hai. Busy-wait wahi galti hai jo low-priority tasks ko CPU se mehroom karti hai. Scheduler aur interrupts chalte rehte hain. Trap: RTOS delay ko super-loop wale busy-wait jaisa samajhna.

questions.question: Inme se hard real-time system ka sabse sahi example kaunsa hai?
options: Music player, jahan kabhi-kabhi halki glitch chal jaati hai
Weather app, jo har ghante data refresh karta hai
Photo gallery, jo scroll karte waqt thumbnails load karti hai
Car ka airbag controller, jahan deadline miss hona failure hai
questions.explanation: Hard real-time me deadline miss = system failure: airbag thodi der se khula to bekaar hai. Music player soft real-time hai (miss se quality girti hai, failure nahi), aur weather app ya gallery me time ki koi strict deadline hi nahi. Trap: 'fast' ko 'hard real-time' samajhna; asli baat deadline ki guarantee hai.

questions.question: RTOS ka tick rate 250 Hz hai. Ek task `delay(50)` call karta hai, jahan argument ticks me hai. Task lagbhag kitni der Blocked rahega?
questions.explanation: 250 Hz par ek tick = 1 ÷ 250 s = 4 ms. 50 ticks × 4 ms = 200 ms (yaani 50 ÷ 250 = 0.2 s). Traps: ticks ko ms maan lena (50 ms, jo 1 kHz tick par sahi hota), 1000 ÷ 50 = 20 ms jaisa ulta divide, ya ticks ko tick rate se multiply karna (50 × 250 ms = 12.5 s).

questions.question: Teen identical DMA channels share karne ke liye ek counting semaphore ka initial count 3 rakha gaya. Paanch tasks lagbhag ek saath `take` karte hain aur abhi koi `give` nahi karta. Kya hoga?
options: Saare 5 tasks ko channel mil jaayega, kyunki semaphore sirf signal hai
Sirf 1 task ko channel milega, baaki 4 Blocked rahenge
3 tasks ko channel milega, baaki 2 Blocked rahenge jab tak koi give na kare
Count -2 ho jaayega aur saare 5 tasks bina ruke chalte rahenge
questions.explanation: Counting semaphore N resources ginta hai: har take count 1 ghatata hai, aur count 0 hone par agla take block hota hai. 3 → 2 → 1 → 0, to teen tasks aage badhte hain aur chautha-paanchwa Blocked rehte hain. 'Sirf 1' binary semaphore/mutex ka behaviour hai, aur count negative hokar sabko nahi chalne deta. Trap: counting aur binary semaphore ko ek samajhna.

questions.question: Preemptive priority scheduler me teen tasks t = 0 par Ready hain: H (priority 3) har 5 ms par 1 ms chalta hai, M (priority 2) har 10 ms par 3 ms chalta hai, aur L (priority 1) background me hamesha Ready hai. Context switch time ignore karo. Pehle 10 ms me M kab khatam hota hai aur L ko kitna CPU milta hai?
options: M t = 3 ms par khatam; L ko 6 ms milte hain
M t = 4 ms par khatam; L ko 5 ms milte hain
M t = 4 ms par khatam; L ko 4 ms milte hain
M t = 5 ms par khatam; L ko 5 ms milte hain
questions.explanation: Timeline: 0–1 H, 1–4 M (M t = 4 par khatam), 4–5 L, 5–6 H (doosri release), 6–10 L. L ko 1 + 4 = 5 ms milte hain; check: 10 − (2 × 1) − 3 = 5. Traps: maan lena ki M pehle chalega (t = 3, L 6 ms), H ki doosri release (t = 5) bhool jaana ya do baar ginna (4 ms), ya M ko H ke doosre run ke baad khatam maanna (t = 5).

questions.question: Teen periodic tasks rate-monotonic priorities ke saath: T1 (C = 2 ms, T = 5 ms), T2 (C = 3 ms, T = 10 ms), T3 (C = 2 ms, T = 20 ms). 3 tasks ka RM bound ≈ 0.78 hai. Sahi conclusion kya hai?
options: U = 0.80; bound se upar, to guarantee nahi, par miss pakka nahi
U = 0.80; bound se zyada, isliye deadlines pakka miss hongi
U = 0.70; bound se kam, isliye RM saari deadlines guarantee karta hai
U = 1.25; 1 se zyada, isliye system pakka overload hai
questions.explanation: U = 2/5 + 3/10 + 2/20 = 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.1 = 0.80. Ye 0.78 se zyada hai, to RM test guarantee nahi deta, par bound sirf sufficient condition hai; U ≤ 1 hai, to tasks phir bhi schedule ho sakte hain (yahan timeline banao to sab deadlines milti hain). Traps: bound se upar ko pakka failure maanna, galat jod (0.70), ya C/T ki jagah T/C ulta lena aur 1.25 jaisa number nikaalna.

questions.question: Queue ki length 3 hai aur shuru me khaali hai. High-priority producer timeout 0 ke saath items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 bhejta hai (beech me consumer nahi chalta). Phir consumer 2 items receive karta hai. Phir producer 6 aur 7 bhejta hai. Ab queue me kaunse items (aage se peeche) hain?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 queue me jaate hain; 4 aur 5 queue full hone par timeout 0 ki wajah se turant fail hote hain (overwrite nahi). Consumer FIFO order me 1 aur 2 nikaalta hai, to sirf 3 bachta hai. Phir 6 aur 7 jagah milne par jud jaate hain: 3, 6, 7. Traps: full queue ko 'oldest overwrite' samajhna (5, 6, 7), failed sends ko baad me queue me maan lena (3, 4, 5), ya 3 ko bhi receive hua maanna (6, 7).

questions.question: Task L (priority 1) t = 0 par mutex leta hai; uske critical section me 3 ms CPU lagta hai. t = 1 ms par H (priority 3) Ready hota hai aur turant usi mutex par block ho jaata hai. t = 1.5 ms par M (priority 2, mutex nahi chahiye) Ready hota hai aur 5 ms CPU leta hai. Context switch ignore karo. H ko mutex kab milega?
options: Inheritance ke saath t = 3 ms; bina inheritance t = 8 ms
Inheritance ke saath t = 3 ms; bina inheritance t = 6.5 ms
Inheritance ke saath t = 1 ms; bina inheritance t = 3 ms
Inheritance ke saath t = 8 ms; bina inheritance t = 3 ms
questions.explanation: Inheritance ke saath: t = 1 par H block hota hai aur L priority 3 le leta hai, to t = 1.5 par M use preempt nahi kar sakta. L ko 2 ms aur chahiye, to t = 3 par mutex chhodta hai. Bina inheritance: L 0–1.5 tak 1.5 ms kar paata hai, phir M 1.5–6.5 chalta hai, phir L baaki 1.5 ms (6.5–8) karta hai: t = 8. Traps: L ke bache 1.5 ms bhool jaana (6.5), H ko L ko preempt karke mutex le lene dena (1 ms; mutex owner hi chhod sakta hai), ya dono cases ulat dena.

weeks.title: Advanced Embedded C: Callbacks, Register Structs and Critical Sections
weeks.summary: Is week aap function pointers aur callbacks, dispatch tables, struct se register map banana, bit-fields aur struct padding ke portability issues, `inline` aur optimisation, aur ISR ke saath shared data ke liye critical sections seekhoge.
concepts: **Function pointers**: `void (*fp)(int);` ka matlab: `fp` ek pointer hai jo aise function ko point karta hai jo `int` leta hai aur kuch return nahi karta. Call: `fp(5);`. Readable banane ke liye `typedef void (*handler_t)(void);`. Cortex-M ki vector table bhi asal me function pointers ki array hai.

**Callbacks**: driver ko ek function pointer de do (jaise `uart_set_rx_callback(on_byte)`), aur event aane par driver use call karta hai. Driver ko application ke baare me kuch pata nahi hota, isliye code loosely coupled rehta hai. Call karne se pehle pointer `NULL` to nahi, ye check karo.
**Dispatch table**: `handler_t table[] = { cmd_a, cmd_b, cmd_c };` aur `table[cmd]();` bade `switch` ki jagah kaam karta hai. Index hamesha range-check karo, warna galat address par jump hoga.

**Struct-based register map**: ek peripheral ke registers lagataar fixed offsets par hote hain, isliye unhe struct se map karte hain: `typedef struct { volatile uint32_t MODER; volatile uint32_t OTYPER; ... } GPIO_Regs;` aur `#define GPIOA ((GPIO_Regs *)0x40020000)`. Ab `GPIOA->ODR` ka address = base + us member ka offset (har `uint32_t` member 4 bytes).

**Bit-fields aur portability**: `struct { uint32_t en : 1; uint32_t mode : 3; }` saaf dikhta hai, par bits LSB se bharenge ya MSB se, padding aur storage unit kya hogi, ye **implementation-defined** hai; compiler ya target badalne par layout badal sakta hai. Bit-field me likhna andar se read-modify-write banta hai, jo kuch hardware registers ke liye khatarnaak hai. Registers ke liye masks aur shifts zyada portable hain.

**Struct padding**: compiler har member ko uske natural alignment par rakhta hai (`uint32_t` 4-byte boundary par) aur struct ke end me bhi padding daal sakta hai. Typical 32-bit ARM par `{ uint8_t a; uint32_t b; uint16_t c; }` = 12 bytes, par members ko bade se chhote order me rakho to 8 bytes. Isliye protocol packet ko seedha struct me cast karna risky hai.

**inline aur optimisation**: `static inline` chhote functions (jaise `led_on()`) ko call overhead ke bina expand karne ka hint deta hai (order nahi). Optimisation (-O2, -Os) code chhota aur fast karta hai, par `volatile` bina wale hardware/ISR variables ke reads/writes hata bhi deta hai, isliye kuch bugs sirf optimised build me dikhte hain.

**Critical section**: `count++` asal me teen steps hai: load, add, store. Agar beech me ISR bhi `count` badle, to ek update kho jaata hai (race condition). Fix: shared data ke operation ke aas-paas interrupts thodi der band karo (Cortex-M par jaise `__disable_irq()`), phir pehle wali state restore karo. Critical section jitna chhota ho sake utna accha, warna interrupt latency badhti hai.

example.problem: Neeche GPIO register struct diya hai, base address 0x40020000 (illustrative). `GPIOA->ODR` kis address par hoga?
steps: Har member `volatile uint32_t` hai, yaani 4 bytes, aur sab bina gap ke lage hain.
Offsets: MODER 0x00, OTYPER 0x04, OSPEEDR 0x08, PUPDR 0x0C, IDR 0x10, ODR 0x14.
ODR chhatha member hai (index 5), offset = 5 × 4 = 20 = 0x14.
Answer: **0x40020014** (wahi address jo week 2 ke `#define GPIOA_ODR` me tha).

mistakes: Register struct me members ko `volatile` na banana. Compiler repeated reads (jaise status poll) ko ek hi read me badal sakta hai.
Bit-field struct ko alag compilers ke beech binary data share karne ke liye use karna. Layout implementation-defined hai; explicit shifts/masks se pack karo.
Critical section me lamba kaam (printf, loops) daalna. Interrupts der tak band rehte hain aur events miss hote hain; sirf shared variable wala chhota hissa protect karo.
revision: `void (*fp)(int);` = int lene wale void function ka pointer.
Callback = driver app ka function pointer call karta hai; `NULL` check.
Register struct: address = base + member offset.
Bit-field layout implementation-defined; registers ke liye masks.
Padding: typical ARM par `{u8, u32, u16}` = 12 bytes.
Shared ISR data par read-modify-write = critical section me.

questions.question: Kaunsa declaration `fp` ko aise function ka pointer banata hai jo ek `int` leta hai aur kuch return nahi karta?
questions.explanation: `(*fp)` ke brackets batate hain ki `fp` pointer hai, aur `(int)` batata hai ki woh jis function ko point karta hai woh int leta hai, return `void`. Bina brackets `void *fp(int);` ek function declare karta hai jo `void *` return karta hai (sabse common trap). `void fp(int *);` int-pointer lene wala function hai, aur `(fp*)` invalid syntax hai.

questions.question: Is register map me `UART1->CR1` kis address par hai?
questions.explanation: Har member 4 bytes ka hai: SR offset 0x0, DR 0x4, BRR 0x8, CR1 0xC. Address = 0x40011000 + 0xC = 0x4001100C. Trap: member ka number (3) seedha bytes me jod dena (0x40011003); struct offsets bytes me hote hain, har `uint32_t` 4 bytes. 0x40011010 agle (paanchve) register ka hota.

questions.question: Hardware register ko bit-field struct se map karna kam portable kyun maana jaata hai?
options: Bit-fields C standard me allowed hi nahi hain
Bit-fields hamesha normal variables se zyada memory lete hain
Bits ka order aur packing implementation-defined hai, isliye compiler ya target badalne par layout badal sakta hai
questions.explanation: C standard bit-fields allow karta hai, par yeh tay nahi karta ki pehla field LSB se shuru hoga ya MSB se, aur unit/padding kaisi hogi. Ek compiler par sahi kaam karne wala register map doosre par galat bits chhu sakta hai. Bit-fields `volatile` ho sakte hain aur aksar memory bachaate hain, isliye baaki options galat hain.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Table ka order `{ c, a, b }` hai: table[0] = c, table[1] = a, table[2] = b. seq = 2, 0, 1, 2 → b, c, a, b → BCAB. Trap: index ko seedha a, b, c ke order se jodna (2 → c, 0 → a ...), jisse CABC aata; table me functions jis order me rakhe hain wahi matter karta hai.

questions.question: Timer ISR har 1 ms par `count++` karta hai, aur main loop kabhi-kabhi `count = count + 10;` karta hai. `count` `volatile uint32_t` hai. Testing me kabhi-kabhi ISR ka ek increment gayab ho jaata hai. Sabse sahi wajah aur fix kya hai?
options: Main ka update load-add-store hai; ISR beech me aaye to uska increment overwrite ho jaata hai. Fix: us statement ke aas-paas interrupts thodi der band karo
`volatile` ki wajah se compiler value cache karta hai. Fix: `volatile` hata do
32-bit variable overflow ho raha hai. Fix: `uint64_t` use karo
ISR ki priority bahut high hai. Fix: use sabse low priority do
questions.explanation: Main `count` ko register me load karta hai, 10 jodta hai, aur store karta hai. Agar load ke baad aur store se pehle ISR chal kar `count++` kare, to main ka store purani value + 10 likh deta hai aur ISR ka +1 kho jaata hai. `volatile` sirf caching rokta hai, atomic nahi banata; ise hatane se problem aur badhegi. Fix: chhota critical section (ya atomic instruction).

questions.question: Typical 32-bit ARM compiler (natural alignment, koi packing attribute nahi) par is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `id` offset 0 par (1 byte), phir `value` ko 4-byte boundary chahiye, isliye 3 bytes padding aur `value` offset 4–7 par. `crc` offset 8–9 par. Struct ka size uske sabse bade alignment (4) ka multiple hona chahiye, isliye end me 2 bytes padding: total 12. Trap: sirf members ke size jodna (1 + 4 + 2 = 7). 8 tab aata jab members `value, crc, id` order me hote.

questions.question: `typedef void (*cb_t)(uint8_t);` ke baad `cb_t` kya hai?
options: Aise function ke pointer ka type jo `uint8_t` leta hai aur kuch return nahi karta
Ek function jo `uint8_t` return karta hai aur koi bhi argument nahi leta
`uint8_t` ka hi ek naya naam, bilkul `typedef uint8_t byte;` jaisa
Ek array ka type jisme `uint8_t` values ke pointers rakhe jaate hain
questions.explanation: `(*cb_t)` batata hai ki ye pointer hai, bahar ka `void ... (uint8_t)` batata hai ki pointed function `uint8_t` leta hai aur `void` return karta hai. `typedef` ise ek type naam bana deta hai, taaki `cb_t on_rx;` likh sako. Trap: return type aur parameter ko ulat padhna, ya `typedef` ko sirf `uint8_t` ka alias samajhna.

questions.question: Driver callback call karne se pehle `if (cb != NULL)` check kyun karta hai?
options: Is check se callback function zyada fast chalta hai aur kam stack leta hai
Agar application ne callback set nahi kiya, to NULL address par jump karke crash hoga
C me function pointer ko bina check kiye call karna compile error deta hai
Ye check callback ko apne aap interrupt-safe aur re-entrant bana deta hai
questions.explanation: Callback optional ho sakta hai; set na ho to pointer NULL rehta hai, aur NULL ko call karna kisi invalid address par jump hai, jo fault ya crash deta hai. Check speed nahi badhata, compiler bina check ke bhi code compile karta hai, aur interrupt-safety alag cheez hai. Trap: maan lena ki compiler aisi galti pakad lega.

questions.question: `static inline` function ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Compiler ko har call hamesha inline karni hi padti hai, chahe function bada ho
Ye function sirf interrupt handlers ke andar se hi call ho sakta hai
Iska matlab hai ki function ka result pehli call ke baad cache ho jaata hai
Ye compiler ko call overhead ke bina code expand karne ka hint hai, order nahi
questions.explanation: `inline` ek suggestion hai; compiler optimisation level aur function size dekh kar decide karta hai ki expand kare ya normal call. `static` use file-private rakhta hai, jo header me chhote helpers (jaise `led_on()`) ke liye common hai. Iska interrupts ya result caching se koi sambandh nahi. Trap: `inline` ko guarantee samajhna.

questions.question: Typical 32-bit ARM compiler (natural alignment, koi packing nahi) par `sizeof(struct s)` kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `b` offset 0 (4 bytes), `c` offset 4 (2 bytes), `a` offset 6 (1 byte): 7 bytes data. Struct ka alignment uske sabse bade member (`uint32_t`, 4) jitna hai, isliye end me 1 byte padding: 8. Traps: tail padding bhool jaana (7), har member ko 4 bytes dena (12), ya `uint32_t` ko 3 bytes ginna (6).

questions.question: Is register map me `TIM->DR` kis address par hoga?
questions.explanation: Offsets: CR 0x00, SR 0x04, RESERVED[0] 0x08, RESERVED[1] 0x0C, DR 0x10. Address = 0x40013000 + 0x10 = 0x40013010. Reserved array hardware ke gap ko bharta hai taaki DR sahi offset par aaye. Traps: reserved words ko na ginna (0x08), reserved array ko ek hi word ginna (0x0C), ya ek extra word jod dena (0x14).

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Trace (total = 1): cmd 0 → `inc(3)` → 4. cmd 1 → `dbl` → 8. cmd 5 range check fail karta hai, skip. cmd 1 → 16. cmd 0 → `inc(4)` → 20. Traps: 5 ko kisi tarah `clr` maan lena (0, phir 0 × 2 + 4 = 4), aakhri `inc` bhool jaana (16), ya 5 ko wrap karke `inc(7)` chalana (15 → 30 → 34). Range check ki wajah se galat index par jump nahi hota.

questions.question: Typical 32-bit ARM compiler (natural alignment) par is struct ka size kya hai, aur members ko bade se chhote order me rakhne par `struct rec log[10];` me kitne bytes bachenge?
questions.explanation: Abhi: `a` 0, padding 1, `b` 2–3, `c` 4, padding 5–7, `d` 8–11 → 12 bytes. Order `d`, `b`, `a`, `c`: offsets 0, 4, 6, 7 → 8 bytes, bina padding. Har element 4 bytes bachata hai, to 10 elements me 40 bytes. Traps: padding ignore karke sirf data (8) ginna, har member ko 4 bytes dena (16), ya bachat 3 bytes per element lena (30).

questions.question: Dono functions main code se chalte hain, aur `buf`/`head` ko ek UART ISR bhi badalta hai. Is code me kya galat hai?
options: Koi bug nahi: `__disable_irq()` do baar call karne se interrupts do levels tak band rehte hain aur sahi jagah khulte hain
Asli bug ye hai ki `head` `volatile` nahi hai; critical section ka is problem se koi lena-dena nahi hai
`log_push()` ka `__enable_irq()` interrupts ko `send_two()` ke beech hi on kar deta hai; pehle wali state save karke restore karni chahiye
Interrupts band karke kisi function ko call karna C me allowed nahi, isliye ye code compile hi nahi hoga
questions.explanation: `__disable_irq()` / `__enable_irq()` koi count nahi rakhte. Pehle `log_push(x)` ke end me `__enable_irq()` interrupts on kar deta hai, to `x` aur `y` ke beech ISR aa kar `head` badal sakta hai, jabki `send_two()` maanta hai ki dono ek atomic block me gaye. Fix: andar wale function me pehle ki interrupt state (PRIMASK) save karo aur end me wahi restore karo. Traps: nesting ko apne aap handled maan lena, `volatile` ko atomicity ka fix samajhna, ya isse compile error sochna.

questions.question: Is register map me `&ADC1->CH[2]` aur `&ADC1->IRQ` ke addresses kya honge?
questions.explanation: CTRL 0x00, STAT 0x04, CH[0] 0x08. Har element 4 bytes, to CH[2] = 0x08 + 2 × 4 = 0x10. CH[4] poora 16 bytes leta hai (0x08–0x17), isliye IRQ 0x18 par. Addresses: 0x40012010 aur 0x40012018. Traps: array index ko bytes me ginna (0x0A aur 0x0C), IRQ ko CH[3] ki jagah rakh dena (0x14), ya CH[2] ko struct ka teesra word samajhna (0x0C).

weeks.title: Tools and Debugging: Build Output, Debug Probes and Watchdogs
weeks.summary: Is week aap build pipeline (compiler, linker, map file), JTAG/SWD debug probe se breakpoints aur watchpoints, oscilloscope aur logic analyser ka sahi use, aur watchdog timer ka timeout calculate karna aur sahi tarah feed karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Build pipeline**: preprocessor (`#include`, `#define`) → compiler (har `.c` file se alag `.o` object) → linker (saare `.o` aur libraries jod kar final addresses assign karta hai) → `.elf` (code + debug symbols) → `.bin`/`.hex` (Flash me jaane wale raw bytes). Syntax error compiler deta hai; 'undefined reference' linker deta hai jab koi function kahin define hi nahi mila.

**Linker script aur map file**: linker script batati hai Flash aur RAM kahan se shuru hain, kitne bade hain, aur kaunsa section kahan jaayega. **Map file** har section aur symbol ka address aur size dikhati hai, jisse memory overflow, sabse badi functions ya galat placement pakde jaate hain. `size` jaisa tool text/data/bss ka total deta hai.

**JTAG vs SWD**: debug probe (jaise ST-LINK) chip ke debug port se judta hai. JTAG me 4–5 pins (TCK, TMS, TDI, TDO, optional TRST) aur kai chips ki daisy-chain. **SWD** (Serial Wire Debug) ARM ka 2-pin interface hai: SWDIO aur SWCLK, Cortex-M par sabse common. Dono se Flash program karna, CPU halt/step karna aur registers/memory dekhna hota hai.

**Breakpoints aur watchpoints**: Flash me chal rahe code ko debugger aasaani se patch nahi kar sakta, isliye core ke **hardware breakpoint** units use hote hain, jo gine-chune hote hain (chip par depend, aksar kuch hi). **Watchpoint** kisi address par read/write hote hi CPU rok deta hai, jisse pata chalta hai kaun sa code variable ko kharab kar raha hai.

**Oscilloscope vs logic analyser**: scope analog waveform dikhata hai: voltage levels, rise time, noise, ringing. Logic analyser kai digital lines ko 0/1 me record karta hai aur UART/SPI/I2C ko decode kar deta hai. Sampling rate signal ki sabse fast frequency se kaafi zyada (kam se kam 4 guna) rakho. Timing naapne ke liye code me ek GPIO toggle karke use scope par dekhna bahut useful trick hai.

**printf debugging ki seemayein**: UART par print aasaan hai, par slow hai aur timing badal deta hai; ISR ya tight loops me isse bug chhup bhi sakta hai. Timing-sensitive bugs ke liye GPIO toggle, trace, ya debugger behtar hain.

**Watchdog timer**: ek independent counter jo time-out hone par MCU reset kar deta hai. Software ko time-out se pehle use 'feed/refresh' karna hota hai. Program hang ho jaaye to feed nahi hoga, reset hoga, aur system recover karega. Timeout = counts × (prescaler ÷ watchdog clock). Feed sirf healthy main path se karo; timer ISR se bina soche feed karna watchdog ko bekaar kar deta hai, kyunki main hang ho tab bhi ISR chalta rehta hai.

**Optimisation se badalne wale bugs**: -O0 (debug) me chalne wala code -O2 me fail ho to pehle check karo: missing `volatile`, uninitialised variables, aur undefined behaviour (jaise array bounds ke bahar likhna).

example.problem: Watchdog ka clock 32 kHz hai, prescaler 64, aur counter 1000 counts ke baad reset karta hai. Timeout kitna hai? Main loop worst-case 1.5 s leta hai aur har iteration me ek baar feed karta hai. Kya reset aayega?
steps: Watchdog counter clock = 32,000 ÷ 64 = 500 Hz, yaani ek count = 2 ms.
Timeout = 1000 counts × 2 ms = 2000 ms = 2 s.
Do feeds ke beech maximum gap = worst-case loop time = 1.5 s.
1.5 s < 2 s, isliye normal operation me reset nahi aayega; 0.5 s ka margin hai.
Answer: **timeout = 2 s; normal chalne par reset nahi**, par loop 2 s se zyada atka to reset.

mistakes: Watchdog ko periodic timer ISR se feed karna. Main loop hang ho jaaye tab bhi ISR feed karta rahega aur watchdog kabhi reset nahi karega.
Watchdog timeout ko worst-case loop time ke bilkul barabar ya kam rakhna. Kabhi-kabhi lamba chalne wale path (Flash erase, retries) par bina wajah reset aate hain; margin rakho.
'undefined reference' ko compiler error samajh kar header file me dhoondhna. Ye linker error hai: function ki definition wali `.c` file ya library build me shaamil karo.
revision: Compiler → `.o`, linker → `.elf` (addresses + symbols), map file = har section/symbol ka address aur size.
SWD = 2 pins (SWDIO, SWCLK); JTAG = 4–5 pins.
Flash code par hardware breakpoints, count limited; watchpoint = data access par stop.
Scope = analog detail, logic analyser = kai digital lines + protocol decode.
Watchdog timeout = counts × prescaler ÷ clock; feed sirf healthy path se.

questions.question: Cortex-M chip ko SWD se debug karne ke liye (GND aur power ke alawa) kaunse do signals chahiye?
questions.explanation: SWD (Serial Wire Debug) sirf do lines use karta hai: SWDIO (bidirectional data) aur SWCLK (clock). Baaki options UART, I2C aur SPI ke signals hain, debug port ke nahi. JTAG ko 4–5 lines chahiye, isliye pin-limited Cortex-M boards par SWD common hai.

questions.question: Build ke dauraan error aaya: "undefined reference to `uart_init`". Ye error kis stage par aata hai?
questions.explanation: Compiler har `.c` file ko alag compile karta hai; agar prototype mil gaya to woh function call ko accept kar leta hai. Linker jab saare `.o` jodta hai aur `uart_init` ki definition kahin nahi milti, tab 'undefined reference' deta hai. Fix: woh `.c` file ya library build me jodo. Trap: header include ko problem samajhna.

questions.question: Watchdog ka clock 40 kHz hai, prescaler 16, aur 500 counts ke baad reset hota hai. Main loop har iteration me ek baar feed karta hai, aur loop ka worst-case time 250 ms hai. Kya hoga?
options: Timeout 2 s hai, koi reset nahi hoga
Timeout 200 ms hai, par loop har baar feed karta hai isliye reset nahi hoga
Timeout 200 ms hai, worst-case loop par watchdog reset kar dega
Timeout 20 ms hai, har iteration me reset hoga
questions.explanation: Counter clock = 40,000 ÷ 16 = 2500 Hz, ek count = 0.4 ms. Timeout = 500 × 0.4 ms = 200 ms. Worst-case me do feeds ke beech 250 ms ka gap hai, jo 200 ms se zyada hai, isliye kabhi-kabhi reset aayega. Trap: 'har loop me feed hai to safe hai' sochna; feed ka gap timeout se chhota hona chahiye, margin ke saath.

questions.question: Logic analyser par UART TX line ki sabse chhoti pulse (ek bit) ki width 104 µs naapi gayi. Baud rate lagbhag kya hai?
questions.explanation: Baud = 1 ÷ bit time = 1 ÷ 104 µs ≈ 9615, yaani standard 9600 baud. 115200 baud par ek bit ≈ 8.68 µs hota. Trap: bit width ko hi baud bol dena (104), ya 10 bits per frame ka factor bit time par laga dena (960).

questions.question: Debugger se Flash me chal rahe code par 10 breakpoints lagane ki koshish ki, par sirf kuch hi lag paaye aur baaki par error aaya. Iski sabse sahi wajah kya hai?
options: Flash me chal rahe code par breakpoint lag hi nahi sakta
SWD protocol sirf 1 breakpoint allow karta hai
Compiler optimisation breakpoints ko delete kar deta hai
Flash code ke liye core ke hardware breakpoint units use hote hain, jo gine-chune hote hain
questions.explanation: RAM me debugger instruction ko ek breakpoint instruction se badal sakta hai (software breakpoint), par Flash me aisa karna practical nahi. Isliye Flash code par core ke hardware comparators use hote hain, aur unki ginti chip par depend karti hai (aksar kuch hi). Breakpoint lagte to hain, bas limited; SWD khud koi '1 breakpoint' limit nahi lagata.

questions.question: Map file se sizes mile: `.text` = 0x3A20, `.rodata` = 0x0400, `.data` = 0x0120, `.bss` = 0x0860 bytes. Linker script RAM me stack ke liye 0x0400 bytes reserve karti hai. MCU me 16 KB Flash aur 4 KB RAM hai. Sahi conclusion kya hai?
options: Flash 15904 bytes, RAM 3456 bytes; dono fit
Flash 16192 bytes, RAM 3456 bytes; dono fit
Flash 16192 bytes, RAM 4480 bytes; RAM overflow
questions.explanation: Flash = text + rodata + data = 0x3A20 + 0x0400 + 0x0120 = 0x3F40 = 16192 bytes, jo 16384 me fit hai (sirf 192 bytes bache). RAM = data + bss + stack = 0x0120 + 0x0860 + 0x0400 = 0xD80 = 3456 bytes, jo 4096 me fit hai. Traps: `.data` ki initial values ko Flash me na ginna (15904), `.bss` ko Flash me jodna (18336), ya `.rodata` ko RAM me bhi gin lena (4480).

questions.question: Code me ek semicolon chhoot gaya hai. Ye error build ke kis stage par pakda jaayega?
questions.explanation: Syntax errors compiler pakadta hai jab wo `.c` file ko parse karta hai; isse `.o` file banti hi nahi. Linker sirf objects jodta hai aur missing definitions ('undefined reference') pakadta hai. Debugger aur programmer build ke baad aate hain. Trap: har build error ko linker ka maan lena.

questions.question: Ek global variable kahin se galat value se overwrite ho raha hai, par pata nahi kaunsa code ye kar raha hai. Sabse direct debugging tool kaunsa hai?
options: Har function ke andar `printf` daal dena
Watchdog ka timeout thoda badha dena
Oscilloscope se power supply ki ripple dekhna
Us variable ke address par write watchpoint
questions.explanation: Watchpoint us address par write hote hi CPU rok deta hai, aur debugger wahi instruction dikhata hai jo likh rahi hai. `printf` har jagah daalna slow hai aur timing badal kar bug chhupa sakta hai. Watchdog aur oscilloscope is sawaal ka jawab nahi dete. Trap: hardware tool ko memory-corruption bug par lagana.

questions.question: Ek SPI bus ki chaaron lines (SCLK, MOSI, MISO, CS) ek saath record karke bytes decode karne hain. Kaunsa instrument sabse sahi hai?
questions.explanation: Logic analyser kai digital lines ek saath 0/1 me record karta hai aur SPI/I2C/UART decode kar deta hai. Ek channel ka scope ek hi line dikhata hai, multimeter average voltage deta hai, aur watchdog debugging instrument hi nahi. Trap: scope ko har signal problem ka jawab samajhna; scope analog detail (noise, ringing) ke liye best hai.

questions.question: Watchdog ka clock 32 kHz hai, prescaler 32, aur reload value 4095 counts hai. Timeout lagbhag kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Counter clock = 32,000 ÷ 32 = 1000 Hz, yaani ek count = 1 ms. Timeout = 4095 × 1 ms ≈ 4.1 s. Traps: prescaler bhool jaana (4095 ÷ 32,000 ≈ 0.13 s), prescaler se divide ki jagah multiply karke ms me ginna (≈ 131 s), ya factor 10 ki galti (0.41 s).

questions.question: Logic analyser se 4 MHz SPI clock record karna hai. 'Kam se kam 4 guna' rule ke hisaab se minimum sampling rate kya honi chahiye?
questions.explanation: Sampling rate ≥ 4 × 4 MHz = 16 MHz, taaki har clock high aur low ke dauraan kam se kam do samples aayein aur edges saaf dikhein. 4 MHz par har period ka ek hi sample hoga aur clock dikhega hi nahi; 8 MHz Nyquist jaisi bare minimum hai jo timing me galtiyaan deti hai; 1 MHz signal se bhi dheema hai. Trap: sampling rate ko signal frequency ke barabar rakhna.

questions.question: Watchdog clock 40 kHz hai, prescaler 4, 8, 16, 32 ya 64 ho sakta hai, aur reload value 12-bit (max 4095) hai. Main loop ka worst-case 2.5 s hai aur timeout lagbhag 3 s chahiye. Kaunsi setting sahi hai?
questions.explanation: Prescaler 32: count = 32 ÷ 40,000 = 0.8 ms, to 3 s ke liye 3000 ÷ 0.8 = 3750 counts, jo 4095 me fit hai. Prescaler 16 (0.4 ms) ke liye 7500 chahiye, jo 12-bit se bada hai. Prescaler 64 ke saath 3750 counts = 6 s, zarurat se double. Prescaler 32 ke saath reload 3000 = 2.4 s, jo 2.5 s ke worst-case loop se kam hai, to normal chalne par bhi reset aa sakta hai. Trap: counts aur time ko mix karna.

questions.question: Ek global table `uint16_t sine[1024] = { ... };` hai. Developer use `const uint16_t sine[1024] = { ... };` bana deta hai (code me koi aur badlaav nahi). Flash aur RAM usage par kya asar padega?
options: Flash 2048 bytes kam hoga, RAM same rahegi
Flash same rahega, RAM 2048 bytes kam ho jaayegi
Flash aur RAM dono 2048 bytes kam honge
Flash 2048 bytes badhega, RAM 2048 bytes kam hogi
questions.explanation: Pehle table `.data` me thi: 1024 × 2 = 2048 bytes initial values Flash me aur 2048 bytes runtime copy RAM me. `const` ke baad wo `.rodata` me hai: sirf Flash me 2048 bytes, RAM me kuch nahi. To Flash ka total wahi, RAM 2048 bytes kam. Traps: maan lena ki `.data` Flash nahi leta (Flash ghatega), dono ko ghata dena, ya `.rodata` ko extra Flash samajhna.

questions.question: 1 ms ke periodic loop me `filter()` ke pehle ek GPIO high aur baad me low kiya gaya. Scope par high pulse 340 µs ka dikhta hai. Ab koi har iteration me 40 characters ka blocking `printf` (UART 115200 baud, 8N1) jodna chahta hai. Sahi analysis kya hai?
options: `filter()` 340 µs leta hai (34% load); printf ≈ 0.35 ms lega, to aaram se fit ho jaayega
`filter()` 660 µs leta hai (66% load); printf ≈ 2.78 ms lega, to fit nahi hoga
`filter()` 340 µs leta hai (34% load); printf ≈ 3.47 ms lega, jo 1 ms period me fit nahi
`filter()` 340 µs leta hai (3.4% load); printf ≈ 3.47 ms lega, phir bhi fit ho jaayega
questions.explanation: High pulse ki width hi `filter()` ka time hai: 340 µs, yaani 1 ms period ka 34%. Printf: 40 × 10 bits = 400 bits ÷ 115,200 ≈ 3.47 ms, jo poore 1 ms period se bhi zyada hai, to loop deadline miss karega. Traps: low time ko function time lena (660 µs), har character ko 1 ya 8 bits ginna (0.35 ya 2.78 ms), ya percentage me factor 10 ki galti (3.4%).

questions.question: `main.c` `adc.h` include karta hai aur `adc_read()` call karta hai; `adc.h` me `uint16_t adc_read(void);` declared hai. `adc.c` (jo `adc.h` include nahi karta) me function `static uint16_t adc_read(void) { ... }` define hai. Build karne par kya hoga?
options: `main.c` compile hi nahi hogi, kyunki compiler ko pata chal jaata hai ki `adc.c` me function `static` hai
Dono files compile hongi, par linker 'undefined reference' dega: `static` function file ke bahar nahi dikhta
Build pass ho jaayega, par runtime par `adc_read()` hamesha garbage ya 0 return karega
Preprocessor error aayega, kyunki `adc.h` ke declaration me `static` nahi likha aur dono mismatch hain
questions.explanation: Har `.c` alag compile hota hai: `main.c` ko header se declaration mil jaata hai, to wo theek compile hoti hai aur `adc_read` ke liye external reference chhodti hai. `adc.c` bhi compile hoti hai, par `static` function ko private (internal) bana deta hai. Link ke waqt koi external `adc_read` nahi milta: 'undefined reference to adc_read'. Traps: compiler ko doosri file ka andar ka haal pata hona maan lena, build pass maanna, ya ise preprocessor ka masla samajhna.

weeks.title: Safe, Tested and Responsible Embedded Engineering
weeks.summary: Is week aap defensive coding, MISRA-C jaisi coding guidelines ka idea, C ke integer pitfalls, fail-safe design, testing ke tareeke, aur ek embedded engineer ki professional aur ethical zimmedariyan seekhoge.
concepts: **Safety-critical systems**: pacemaker, car brakes, insulin pump, aircraft controls: yahan bug ka matlab kisi ki jaan ka khatra ho sakta hai. Aise domains ke standards (jaise industrial ke liye IEC 61508, automotive ke liye ISO 26262) process, testing aur documentation maangte hain. Engineer ka kaam hai risks pehchaanna aur unhe design se kam karna.

**Defensive coding**: har input validate karo (range, `NULL`, length), function ke return values check karo, array index ki bounds check karo, `switch` me `default` rakho, aur har hardware wait par timeout lagao: koi bhi loop jo 'flag aane tak' ruke, hamesha ke liye atak sakta hai. 'Impossible' conditions ke liye `assert` debug builds me bugs jaldi pakadta hai.

**MISRA-C ka idea**: C ka ek safer subset (guidelines) jo risky features ko limit karta hai: dynamic memory (`malloc`/`free`) aur recursion avoid, har `if ... else if` chain ke end me `else`, implicit signed/unsigned conversions par dhyaan, `goto` restricted. Static analysis tools in rules ko automatically check karte hain. Exact rule numbers nahi, 'kyun' samjho: predictable, analysable code.

**Integer pitfalls**: signed aur unsigned compare karne par signed value unsigned me convert hoti hai, isliye `-1 < 1U` false hai. Overflow, zero se divide, aur type width ke barabar ya zyada shift bhi galat results dete hain. Compiler warnings (`-Wall -Wextra`) on rakho aur warnings ko errors jaisa treat karo.

**Fail-safe design**: fault aane par system ek **safe state** me jaaye: motor off, valve band, heater off. Iske tools: watchdog, brown-out detection, sensor plausibility checks (out-of-range reading = fault), redundant sensors, aur reset par safe default outputs. 'Last good value par chalte raho' aksar unsafe hota hai.

**Testing**: unit tests (PC par, HAL ko mock karke), **boundary value testing** (limit par aur limit ke just andar/bahar), integration tests, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), aur fault injection (sensor nikaal do, corrupt message bhejo). Code review aur static analysis bugs ko hardware tak pahunchne se pehle pakadte hain.

**Ethics aur professional practice**: safety problem ko chhupao mat aur deadline ke pressure me testing skip mat karo. Apni limits honestly batao. Connected devices me security (default passwords, bina signature ke firmware updates) aur user privacy ka dhyaan rakho. Requirements → design → tests ki traceability aur saaf documentation rakho, taaki koi bhi verify kar sake ki system kya karta hai.

example.problem: Function `set_motor_speed(int pct)` motor ki PWM duty set karta hai. Valid range 0–100 hai. Ise defensive tarah se likho.
steps: Pehle input check karo: `pct < 0` ya `pct > 100` ho to kuch mat badlo aur error return karo.
Silently clamp karne ke bajay error return karna behtar hai, taaki caller ka bug chhupe nahi.
Valid input par duty set karo: CCR = pct × (ARR + 1) ÷ 100.
Success par 0 return karo, aur caller is return value ko check kare.
Answer: **validate → reject with error → tabhi hardware likho**.

mistakes: Hardware flag ke liye bina timeout ke `while` loop likhna. Device disconnect hote hi poora system atak jaata hai; timeout counter aur error path rakho.
Signed aur unsigned ko compare karna aur warning ignore karna. Negative value bahut bada unsigned number ban jaata hai aur condition ulti ho jaati hai.
Sensor fault par 'last good value' se control chalate rehna. Fault pehchaano aur safe state me jaao.
revision: Har input validate, har return value check, har wait par timeout.
MISRA idea: dynamic memory/recursion avoid, final `else`, conversions par dhyaan.
`int` aur `unsigned` compare → int unsigned ban jaata hai.
Fault → safe state (motor off, valve band).
Boundary tests: limit par aur limit ke just bahar.

questions.question: Ek heater controller ka temperature sensor disconnect ho jaata hai aur 12-bit ADC lagataar 4095 (full-scale) padh raha hai, jo is system me physically possible nahi. Sabse sahi fail-safe response kya hai?
options: Heater band karo aur fault indicate karo
Aakhri valid reading ke saath heater chalate raho
Heater ko full power par chala do
Reading ignore karke temperature 25 °C maan lo
questions.explanation: Out-of-range reading sensor fault ka sign hai. Heater ke liye safe state 'off' hai, kyunki bina sahi temperature ke heating jaari rakhna overheating ya aag ka risk hai. Last valid value ya koi made-up value (25 °C) maan kar chalana fault ko chhupata hai. Full power sabse unsafe choice hai.

questions.question: Safety-critical embedded C (jaise MISRA-style guidelines) me dynamic memory (`malloc`/`free`) aksar avoid kyun kiya jaata hai?
options: `malloc` C standard library ka hissa nahi hai
`malloc` hamesha zero se bhari memory deta hai, jo slow hai
Fragmentation aur unpredictable timing/allocation failure ki wajah se behaviour deterministic aur analysable nahi rehta
`malloc` sirf operating system wale computers par kaam karta hai
questions.explanation: Lambe samay tak chalne wale device me baar-baar allocate/free se heap fragment hota hai, aur kisi din allocation fail ho sakti hai, ya uska time badal sakta hai. Ye pehle se prove karna mushkil hai. Static (compile-time) allocation se memory usage fixed aur analysable rehta hai. `malloc` standard ka hissa hai aur bare-metal par bhi chalta hai, isliye A aur D galat; zero se bharna `calloc` karta hai.

questions.question: Is function ke bounds check me kya bug hai?
options: Koi bug nahi, check bilkul sahi hai
`i > N` ki jagah `i >= N` hona chahiye; i = 8 par buf[8] me out-of-bounds write hota hai
`i < 0` wala check galat hai, use hata dena chahiye
Return values ulte hain: success par -1 aana chahiye
questions.explanation: 8 elements ke array ke valid indices 0 se 7 hain. Check `i > N` sirf 9 aur upar ko rokta hai, to i = 8 pass ho jaata hai aur buf[8] array ke bahar likhta hai, jo kisi doosre variable ko kharab kar sakta hai. Sahi: `if (i < 0 || i >= N)`. Negative index check zaroori hai, aur return convention (0 success) theek hai.

questions.question: Function `set_level(int x)` ka valid input range 0 se 100 (dono shaamil) hai; baaki inputs reject hone chahiye. Boundary value testing ke liye sabse accha test set kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: Bugs aksar limits par hote hain (jaise `>` vs `>=`). Isliye har boundary par aur uske just bahar test karo: -1 (reject), 0 (accept), 100 (accept), 101 (reject). Sirf 0 aur 100 test karne se off-by-one wala reject bug pakda nahi jaata. Beech ki values ya bahut door ki values boundary ko test hi nahi karti.

questions.question: Ek I2C driver me ye code hai. Agar sensor ka wire nikal jaaye aur ACK kabhi na aaye, to kya hoga aur behtar design kya hai?
options: Loop hamesha ke liye atak jaayega; timeout counter lagao aur error return karke recovery karo
Hardware khud ACK flag set kar dega, isliye koi problem nahi
Compiler is loop ko optimise karke hata dega kyunki body khaali hai
Loop ek iteration ke baad apne aap ruk jaata hai
questions.explanation: Flag kabhi set nahi hoga, to `while` hamesha chalta rahega aur poora firmware (ya ek RTOS task) atak jaayega; watchdog ho to reset loop ban sakta hai. Har hardware wait par timeout lagao (counter ya tick-based) aur error return karo taaki upar wala code bus reset ya fault report kar sake. Register `volatile` hai, isliye compiler loop nahi hata sakta (trap).

questions.question: 32-bit `int` wale target par is code ka output kya hoga?
options: Undefined behaviour, kuch bhi print ho sakta hai
questions.explanation: `int` aur `unsigned int` compare karne par C ke usual arithmetic conversions `temp` ko unsigned me badal dete hain: -5 ban jaata hai 2³² − 5 = 4294967291, jo 10 se bada hai. Isliye condition false aur TOO HIGH print hota hai. Ye conversion well-defined hai (undefined nahi), aur compiler sirf sign-compare warning deta hai. Trap: maths ki tarah -5 < 10 maan kar OK bolna. Fix: dono ko same signed type me compare karo.

questions.question: Release se ek din pehle aapko pata chalta hai ki ek rare case me infusion pump ka sensor fault detect nahi hota. Professional tareeka kya hai?
options: Issue document karo, team aur manager ko turant batao, aur fix-testing plan banao
Chup raho, kyunki case rare hai aur release ki deadline is waqt zyada important hai
Release notes se us feature ka zikr hata do par code waisa hi rehne do
Bug ko agle version tak chhupa kar rakho taaki launch bina ruke ho jaaye
questions.explanation: Medical device me fault detect na hona kisi ki jaan ke liye khatra hai. Safety problem ko chhupana ya deadline ke pressure me skip karna unethical hai; sahi raasta hai issue document karna, turant escalate karna aur fix verify karna. 'Rare' hone se risk khatam nahi hota. Trap: schedule ko safety se upar rakhna.

questions.question: Compiler warnings (jaise `-Wall -Wextra` se) ke saath safety-critical code me sabse achhi practice kya hai?
options: Warnings band kar do taaki build output saaf dikhe
Warnings on rakho aur unhe errors jaisa treat karke fix karo
Sirf woh warnings dekho jo linker deta hai, compiler ki nahi
Warnings ignore karo jab tak program sahi chalta dikhe
questions.explanation: Warnings aksar asli bugs dikhate hain: signed/unsigned compare, uninitialised variables, unused results. Unhe errors jaisa treat karne se ye bugs hardware tak nahi pahunchte. Band karna ya 'chal to raha hai' soch kar ignore karna problem chhupata hai. Trap: warning ko cosmetic samajhna.

questions.question: Testing me jaan-boojh kar sensor ka cable nikaal diya jaata hai ya corrupt message bheja jaata hai, ye dekhne ke liye ki system safe state me jaata hai ya nahi. Is testing ko kya kehte hain?
questions.explanation: Fault injection me jaan-boojh kar faults (disconnect, corrupt data, power glitch) daal kar dekhte hain ki system unhe pehchaan kar safe state me jaata hai. Boundary testing input ki limits check karti hai, code review insaan code padhte hain, aur benchmarking speed naapti hai. Trap: har 'unusual input' test ko boundary testing kehna.

questions.question: Is loop ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Loop kabhi khatam nahi hoga: `uint8_t` hamesha >= 0 hai, 0 ke baad 255 banta hai
Loop 11 baar chalega, i = 10 se i = 0 tak, aur phir normally ruk jaayega
Loop sirf 10 baar chalega, kyunki i = 0 hote hi condition false ho jaati hai
Compile error aayega, kyunki `uint8_t` variable ko ghataya nahi ja sakta
questions.explanation: Unsigned value kabhi negative nahi hoti, isliye `i >= 0` hamesha true hai. i = 0 par `i--` wrap karke 255 bana deta hai aur loop phir se chalta rehta hai. Signed `int` hota to loop 11 baar chal kar rukta. Compiler aksar is par warning bhi deta hai ('comparison is always true'). Trap: signed loop ka hisaab unsigned par lagana.

questions.question: Is function me sabse bada defensive-coding issue kya hai?
options: Loop `i <= n` tak chalna chahiye, warna array ka aakhri element chhoot jaayega
`const` lagane se array padha nahi ja sakta, isliye use hata dena chahiye
Function `int` return karta hai, isliye isme koi problem ho hi nahi sakti
`n == 0` par zero se divide hoga aur `a` NULL ho sakta hai; pehle dono check karo
questions.explanation: Khaali array (n = 0) aane par `s / n` zero se divide hai, jo MCU par fault de sakta hai; aur NULL pointer se padhna bhi crash hai. Defensive version pehle `a == NULL || n <= 0` check karke error return karta hai. `i < n` bilkul sahi hai (`<=` ek element bahar padhega), aur `const` sirf likhne se rokta hai, padhne se nahi. Trap: off-by-one ko 'fix' karke asli bug bana dena.

questions.question: 32-bit `int` wale target par is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `int` aur `unsigned int` compare karne par `int` unsigned me convert hota hai. -3 ban jaata hai 4294967293, jo 10 se bada hai, to count hota hai. 5 > 10 false, 12 > 10 true. Count = 2. Traps: normal maths ki tarah sochna (sirf 12, to 1), sab ko bada maan lena (3), ya maan lena ki negative value comparison ko hi tod deti hai (0). Fix: `lim` ko `int` rakho ya pehle negative check karo.

questions.question: Har call me READY bit pehli 3 reads par 0 aur 4th read par 1 milta hai. `wait_ready(3)` aur `wait_ready(5)` kya return karenge?
questions.explanation: `wait_ready(3)`: read 1 (0) → n = 1, read 2 (0) → n = 2, read 3 (0) → n = 3, aur 3 ≥ 3 to -1 (timeout). `wait_ready(5)`: teen reads 0 dete hain (n = 1, 2, 3, koi bhi 5 tak nahi), 4th read par READY 1 hai, loop rukta hai aur n = 3 return hota hai. Traps: maan lena ki check increment se pehle hota hai (jaise `n++ >= max_loops`), jisse `wait_ready(3)` bhi 4th read tak pahunch kar 3 deta (3 aur 3); n ko reads ki ginti samajhna (4); ya maan lena ki pehli 3 zero reads dono calls ko timeout kara dengi (-1 aur -1).

questions.question: Heater ke do temperature sensors A aur B hain. Rule: agar koi reading 0–150 °C ke bahar ho, ya |A − B| > 5 °C ho, to fault maan kar heater band karo. Chaar cases: (1) A = 72, B = 75; (2) A = 80, B = 88; (3) A = 151, B = 149; (4) A = 40, B = 44. Kin cases me heater band hoga?
questions.explanation: Case 1: dono range me, fark 3 ≤ 5: OK. Case 2: fark 8 > 5: fault (sensors aapas me nahi milte). Case 3: fark sirf 2, par A = 151 range ke bahar: fault. Case 4: fark 4 ≤ 5: OK. To heater 2 aur 3 me band. Traps: sirf difference check karna (case 3 miss), sirf range check karna (case 2 miss), ya 4 ke fark ko bhi fault ginna.

questions.question: Memory me ek bit-flip se `m` ki value 7 ho jaati hai. `duty_for(1)` aur `duty_for(7)` kya return karenge, aur safety ke hisaab se sahi fix kya hai?
options: 30 aur 0; `switch` kisi bhi invalid value par apne aap 0 return kar deta hai
30 aur 80; invalid value hamesha aakhri `case` me chali jaati hai
100 aur 100; `switch` `int` argument par kaam nahi karta, isliye d badalta hi nahi
30 aur 100; corrupt value par heater full power par chalega, `default:` me safe value 0 do
questions.explanation: `duty_for(1)` HEAT_LOW case me jaata hai: 30. 7 kisi case se match nahi karta aur koi `default` nahi, to d apni shuruaati value 100 par rehta hai: heater full power, jo sabse unsafe output hai. Defensive fix: `default: d = 0;` (aur fault report), aur initial value bhi safe rakho. Traps: maan lena ki `switch` khud 0 deta hai, invalid value aakhri case me girti hai, ya `int` par `switch` nahi chalta.
